title: go_templates
summary: MSUI mirrors the ask-once GameObject template cache, exact type-to-lock slot mapping and Lock.dbc-driven use/cast routing. Template names and GENERIC data[1] now feed shared world hover, and the first cursor lock type selects PickLock/GatherHerbs/Mine with exact inability rules. Tracked-resource matching is live; MO_TRANSPORT timetable consumption remains open.

openItems.text: GO template name/highlight never feeds a world hover: no GameObject mouseover tooltip and no GENERIC (type 5) data[1] highlight-eligibility gate, since GameObjects are not hover-pickable at all
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: Dynamic GameObjects own a shared world tooltip from their queried template name, and GENERIC type 5 objects are only pick/highlight eligible when template data[1] opts in.

openItems.text: LockType.dbc cursor-stem chain (PickLock/GatherHerbs/Mine cursor over lockable nodes) has no counterpart - there is no contextual world cursor for GameObjects
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: WorldCursorUiLaw consumes LockCatalog's first cursor lock type and selects PickLock, GatherHerbs or Mine with Benilla's lock/range inability semantics.

openItems.text: MO_TRANSPORT (type 15) data0..2 taxiPathId/moveSpeed/accelRate is parsed into Data[] but never consumed - no transport timetable exists
